::: {.callout-note}
## On the roadmap
This page will map transferable skills across the four-year degree,
showing where each is introduced, practised, and expected. The proposed
vocabulary below is the starting point; the next step is to co-develop
it with the department instructor cohort, tag each Freshwater Science
course, and render the coverage as a skills-by-year heatmap. The
[roadmap](#roadmap) at the foot of this page sets out the sequence.
:::

# The idea

Skills get **scaffolded** through a degree: introduced in one course,
practised in several, and expected as background in upper-year courses.
Without an explicit map, neither students nor instructors can see this
arc clearly. The aim of this page is to make that scaffolding visible as
a heatmap, skills on the rows, the four years on the columns, cells
coloured by introduce / practise / expect status.

# Proposed skill vocabulary

Three top-level skill families to start, each with sub-skills, as a
starting point to be refined with the department instructor cohort.

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-md-4 .g-col-12}

### Quantitative / computational
- R basics
- R intermediate (tidyverse)
- R for hydrology (tidyhydat, dataRetrieval)
- Statistical inference
- Geostatistics
- Spatial analysis (sf, terra)
- Modelling (GLM, GAM)

:::

::: {.g-col-md-4 .g-col-12}

### Field / lab
- Sampling design
- Water-quality sampling
- Macroinvertebrate identification
- Hydrometric measurement
- Lab safety
- Calibration and QC

:::

::: {.g-col-md-4 .g-col-12}

### Communication / professional
- Scientific writing
- Public-facing communication
- Peer review
- Project management
- Ethics
- Working with First Nations

:::

:::

# Roadmap {#roadmap}

1. Co-develop the controlled skill vocabulary with the program
   instructor cohort.
2. Tag each Freshwater Science course with the skills it introduces,
   practises, and expects.
3. Render the skills-by-year heatmap from those tags.
